placements.title: authority claimed to command what knowledge is purged from memory or record
placements.frame: Is this directive claiming authority to dictate what the recipient must forget or remove, and what does that reveal about knowledge governance and retention risk in the engagement?
placements.why: Both existing graph structure and strata are empty for this repo, and neither the map nor the area index (ns__Decision_KnowledgeMapping, ns__Actor_XenaGithubber) covers a theme of commanding erasure of knowledge — so there is nothing to reuse. The content itself is not a one-time fact about a specific fleet or route (those named entities have zero correlate anywhere in the graph and are not themselves a recurring subject); rather, both segments instantiate the same recurring pattern the position pass already isolated as MandateToEraseKnowledge — an actor exercising authority to compel what knowledge is retained or purged. That pattern (directives demanding forgetting/removal of held knowledge) is exactly the kind of subject a knowledge-mapping engagement keeps encountering and future envelopes can keep feeding, satisfying the narrative grain test as a theme rather than a fact. No existing hub or strata name is close enough to warrant lineage, so this mints standalone with no forced parent.
